title: When the Tide Breaks
premise: Ivo Okafor, a widowed single parent keeping the coastal town's last bookshop afloat, agrees to pose as the date of bakery owner Marisol Vane at her family's reunion to deflect her grandmother's meddling — but the fake romance turns real just as Marisol inherits controlling shares in the family development company, which plans to raze the harbor block housing both their businesses. Torn between the career that finally earned her family's respect and the man who makes her feel seen, Marisol publicly defies the demolition vote, sacrificing her inheritance to save the street. In the end, she and Ivo merge the bookshop and bakery into one storefront, choosing love and community over legacy and power.
about_author: U. M. Delacroix is the pen name of a former small-town bookseller who now writes slow-burn romances set in fading seaside communities. They live near the Atlantic with two cats and an unhealthy attachment to secondhand paperbacks.

chapters.title: Salt on the Spines
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. We meet Ivo balancing ledger books, his daughter Amara's school forms, and a landlord's warning that the harbor block lease is up for review. The emotional beat is quiet desperation masked by routine warmth as he closes the shop on another thin day.

chapters.title: Flour and Ash
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol burns a batch of sourdough while rehearsing excuses for her grandmother's reunion invitation. A letter arrives: Grandmother Odette is naming an heir to Vane Development. The beat is dread dressed as ambition.

chapters.title: The Proposition
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Marisol barges into the bookshop with an offer: be her fake date for the reunion weekend so her family stops matchmaking her with the company's golden boy, Theo. Ivo refuses; Amara, eavesdropping, accepts on his behalf. Beat: reluctant comedy.

chapters.title: Terms and Conditions
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Over cinnamon rolls, they negotiate rules — no real feelings, split expenses, one weekend only. Ivo notices how tired Marisol looks behind her bravado. Beat: guarded tenderness disguised as contract law.

chapters.title: Arrival at Wren House
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. The reunion begins at the Vane estate: cold marble, colder cousins, and Theo's knowing smirk. Ivo plays his role too well, charming even Odette. Beat: impostor anxiety curdling into unexpected belonging.

chapters.title: Dessert Changes Everything
chapters.summary: Dual POV. During dessert, Odette announces the heir will be revealed Sunday — and that Marisol's 'boyfriend' must stay through it. On the terrace afterward, a near-kiss under string lights breaks rule one. Beat: the fake becomes dangerously plausible.

chapters.title: Sunday's Verdict
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Odette names Marisol heir apparent, contingent on board approval of the Harborline Project — the redevelopment that would demolish the bookshop block. Marisol says nothing. Beat: triumph laced with horror.

chapters.title: The Weight of Paper
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Back home, Ivo learns the lease termination notice is tied to Harborline. He doesn't tell Marisol, ashamed of what her inheritance means for him. Beat: silence as self-protection.

chapters.title: Amara's Map
chapters.summary: Amara's POV (interlude). Eleven-year-old Amara draws a map of the harbor block — bookshop, bakery, the pier where her mother's ashes were scattered — and pins it above Ivo's desk. Beat: grief and hope braided together.

chapters.title: Boardroom Ghosts
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol attends her first board meeting and discovers the Harborline vote is already scheduled — and that her grandmother expects her to deliver it. Theo offers to 'handle' dissent. Beat: power's seductive arithmetic.

chapters.title: What the Tide Keeps
chapters.summary: Dual POV. A storm strands Ivo and Marisol at the bakery overnight; flour-dusted honesty follows. She admits she wants the respect she's starved for; he admits the lease crisis without naming her family. Beat: intimacy built on half-truths.

chapters.title: The First Crack
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo finds the demolition blueprints with the bookshop circled in red — Vane Development letterhead. He walks out mid-argument when Marisol defends the project's jobs. Beat: betrayal arriving ahead of explanation.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Gambit
chapters.summary: Odette's POV (interlude). Odette reveals she engineered the romance rumor to test Marisol: love or legacy, choose. Flashbacks show Odette's own sacrificed marriage. Beat: the corruptor humanized, unrepentant.

chapters.title: Rules of Engagement
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol confronts Ivo; he returns the contract, torn in half. She realizes she defended the project because backing down means proving Odette right about her weakness. Beat: pride as armor over heartbreak.

chapters.title: Theo's Leverage
chapters.summary: Theo's POV (brief). Theo leaks photos of Ivo and Marisol's 'contract' to the family, framing Marisol as a fraud unfit to lead. Beat: villainy as ambition wearing a friendly face.

chapters.title: Public Reading
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. At a town hall on Harborline, Ivo speaks for the block — not attacking Marisol, but describing what the street means to people like Amara. Marisol watches from the back. Beat: love expressed as principle.

chapters.title: The Vote
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Board vote day. Marisol stands, tears up her prepared endorsement, and votes against Harborline, forfeiting the inheritance. Odette's face goes to stone; Theo moves to seize control. Beat: climax — the choice made aloud.

chapters.title: Aftermath of a Name
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Disowned but free, Marisol finds Ivo closing the shop. No speeches — just her hands in flour and his in dust as they inventory what remains. Beat: raw reconciliation without guarantees.

chapters.title: Lease Terms, Revised
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. With the block saved but businesses fragile, Ivo proposes merging bookshop and bakery into one storefront. Amara designs the sign. Beat: rebuilding as courtship.

chapters.title: Odette's Last Ledger
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Dying Odette summons Marisol, leaving her a personal bequest — her mother's recipe box and a grudging admission that Marisol chose correctly. Beat: inheritance redefined as memory, not money.

chapters.title: Opening Day
chapters.summary: Dual POV. 'Tide & Tome' opens: shelves between ovens, Amara at the register, the town crowding in. Theo's rival venture fails quietly offshore. Beat: joy earned, community as reward.

chapters.title: Second Chances, Better Timing
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. One year later, on the pier at dusk, Ivo proposes with a ring hidden in a first-edition of Marisol's favorite novel. She says yes before he finishes. Final beat: timing, at last, is theirs.
